remark.replace: 💡 [Frame $1] SIP INVITE initiates a call — carries SDP offer with codec/media proposals; callee responds with 180 Ringing, then 200 OK with SDP answer
💡 [Frame $1] SIP REGISTER binds a contact URI to an AOR (Address of Record) at the registrar; Expires=0 means unregister; 401 triggers Digest auth challenge
💡 [Frame $1] SIP BYE terminates an established dialog — both sides send BYE to release media resources; Reason header explains why (e.g., user hangup)
💡 [Frame $1] 401 Unauthorized — server challenges client with Digest auth (realm + nonce); client must retry with computed response hash using shared secret
💡 [Frame $1] 407 Proxy Auth Required — SIP proxy challenges the request; same Digest auth flow as 401 but for proxy-level authentication
💡 [Frame $1] 486 Busy Here — callee's device is busy; caller hears busy tone; call may be forwarded if CFNB (Call Forward No Busy) is configured
💡 [Frame $1] 5xx Server Error — proxy or UAS failure; 500=Internal Error, 503=Service Unavailable (overloaded); client should retry with exponential backoff
💡 [Frame $1] 6xx Global Failure — 600=Busy Everywhere (all endpoints busy), 603=Decline (callee explicitly rejected); no point trying other contacts
💡 [Frame $1] 100 Trying — proxy accepted the request and is searching for the callee; stops retransmission timer; no end-to-end significance
💡 [Frame $1] 180 Ringing — callee's phone is alerting; caller hears locally generated ringback; 183 with SDP offers early media (in-band ringback) instead
💡 [Frame $1] 183 Session Progress — carries SDP answer for early media (ringback tone, IVR prompts); RTP flows before call is answered; requires PRACK if 100rel is negotiated
💡 [Frame $1] 200 OK — call answered (for INVITE) or registration accepted (for REGISTER); SDP answer completes codec negotiation; caller must send ACK to complete 3-way handshake
💡 [Frame $1] 3xx Redirect — callee moved; Contact header contains new URI; 301=permanent (update AOR), 302=temporary (try once), 305=use specified proxy
💡 [Frame $1] 180 Ringing — callee's phone is alerting; caller hears locally generated ringback
💡 [Frame $1] 183 Session Progress — early media with SDP answer; RTP flows before call is answered
💡 [Frame $1] 200 OK — call answered or registration accepted; SDP answer completes codec negotiation; ACK required to complete INVITE 3-way handshake
💡 [Frame $1] DTMF digit sent as RTP Named Telephone Event (RFC 4733) — out-of-band signaling preserves digit accuracy across codec transcoding
💡 [Frame $1] RTCP Sender Report — media sender reports packet/byte counts and NTP timestamp for lip-sync; receivers use this to calculate jitter and loss
💡 [Frame $1] RTCP Receiver Report — reports packet loss fraction and jitter for each source; high jitter or loss indicates network congestion affecting voice quality
💡 [Frame $1] SCCP OffHook — phone notifies CUCM the handset is lifted; CUCM responds with dial tone (StartTone) and prepares to collect digits
💡 [Frame $1] SCCP OnHook — handset replaced; CUCM tears down media channels (StopMediaTransmission, CloseReceiveChannel) and releases the call
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM pushes call state to phone — OffHook/Proceed/RingOut/Connected/OnHook; phone updates display and soft keys accordingly
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM sends caller/called party info for phone display; callType (InBound/OutBound) and security status (Authenticated/Encrypted) update the lock icon
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM tells phone to open an RTP receive channel with specified codec and packetization; phone responds with OpenReceiveChannelAck containing its IP:port
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM tells phone where to send RTP — remote IP:port is the other phone's receive address; codec must match the negotiated type
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM tears down the RTP channel — phone stops sending/receiving media; happens on call disconnect, hold, or codec change
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM tells phone to play a tone — InsideDialTone (ready for digits), AlertingTone (ringback), BusyTone, ReorderTone (fast busy = route failure)
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM controls the physical ringer — RingOff on answer/cancel, InsideRing for internal calls, OutsideRing for external; distinctive ring identifies call source
💡 [Frame $1] Phone sends collected digits to CUCM — CUCM matches against dial plan (route patterns, translation patterns) to determine call routing
💡 [Frame $1] SCCP RegisterReq — phone sends its device name (SEP + MAC), IP address, and protocol version to CUCM; CUCM responds with RegisterAck and begins provisioning
💡 [Frame $1] SCCP RegisterAck — CUCM accepts the phone; follows with CapabilitiesReq, ButtonTemplate, SoftKeyTemplate to provision the phone's features
💡 [Frame $1] CUCM asks phone for supported codecs (G.711, G.722, G.729); phone replies with its codec list; CUCM uses this for region-based codec selection during calls
💡 [Frame $1] Phone provisioning — CUCM sends button layout (line/speed-dial/BLF), soft key labels, and device configuration; phone renders its UI from these templates
💡 [Frame $1] Phone queries directory number (DN) for each line button; CUCM responds with the DN, display name, and voicemail settings
💡 [Frame $1] Call forwarding status — phone queries/receives CFA (Call Forward All), CFB (Busy), CFNA (No Answer) settings per line
💡 [Frame $1] H.225 Setup — initiates an H.323 call; carries called/calling numbers, bearer capability, and H.245 address for media negotiation
💡 [Frame $1] Call Proceeding — gateway accepted the Setup and is routing the call; H.245 address may be included for early media negotiation
💡 [Frame $1] Alerting — remote phone is ringing; caller hears ringback tone; Progress indicator may signal in-band audio available
💡 [Frame $1] Connect — call answered; media channel is now established; both sides exchange RTP audio/video on negotiated ports
💡 [Frame $1] Release Complete — call terminated; Cause value explains why (16=Normal clearing, 17=User busy, 34=No circuit available)
💡 [Frame $1] Facility — mid-call supplementary service (hold, transfer, conference); also used for H.245 tunneling and call diversion
